story.title: Six Nigerians Extradited to the US for $6 Million Romance Scam
story.summary: Six Nigerian nationals, allegedly part of the Black Axe criminal network, have been extradited to the United States from South Africa. They are accused of defrauding American women out of over $6 million through online romance scams. The extradition was confirmed by South African police and took place on Friday.

event_overview.title: About Romance Scams
event_overview.subject: Romance Scams
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the extradition from South Africa to the United States of six Nigerian nationals accused of participating in a Cape Town-based online-fraud operation. U.S. prosecutors allege that the operation used false online identities and purported romantic relationships, among other schemes, to obtain and launder victims’ money; the allegations have not been adjudicated and the defendants are presumed innocent.

facts.label: Alleged scheme period
facts.value: The U.S. charges describe an alleged conspiracy operating from at least 2011 through 2021.

facts.label: Locations and court
facts.value: The alleged operation was based in Cape Town, South Africa, targeted victims in the United States, and was charged in two federal cases before the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey in Trenton.

facts.label: Participants
facts.value: The underlying 2021 U.S. announcement charged eight Nigerian nationals, including alleged leaders of the Cape Town Zone of the Neo Black Movement of Africa, also known as Black Axe; South African authorities said six nationals were being transferred in September 2026.

facts.label: Alleged conduct and losses
facts.value: Authorities allege the defendants used romance scams and advance-fee schemes, as well as laundering connected to business-email-compromise fraud; South African authorities said more than 100 U.S. women were allegedly defrauded of over R100 million, reported as more than $6 million.

facts.label: Legal and extradition process
facts.value: The principal U.S. allegations include wire-fraud conspiracy and money-laundering conspiracy; the defendants were arrested in South Africa in 2021, and the Hawks and INTERPOL South Africa facilitated their September 2026 handover to U.S. authorities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the September 11–12, 2026 extradition developments, not the full history of the alleged fraud network, all related defendants, or the eventual U.S. court outcomes.

related_stories.title: US Commemorates 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Attacks with Remembrance Ceremonies
related_stories.summary: On the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, Americans gathered in solemn remembrance of the nearly 3,000 lives lost. Ceremonies took place at significant sites including Ground Zero in New York, the Pentagon, and Shanksville, Pennsylvania, where families, survivors, and first responders reflected on the impact of that tragic day. A new memorial at the Pentagon aims to honor the 184 victims killed there.

related_stories.title: Lil Durk Found Not Guilty in Murder-for-Hire Trial
related_stories.summary: Lil Durk, a Grammy-winning rapper from Chicago, has been acquitted by a federal jury in Los Angeles of charges related to a murder-for-hire plot against rival rapper Quando Rondo. The trial followed his arrest in 2024, stemming from accusations linked to a shooting that resulted in the death of Rondo's cousin.

related_stories.title: Investigation Underway After Train Derails in France, Injuring 44
related_stories.summary: A train derailed in Normandy, France, injuring 44 people, including one in critical condition. Authorities suspect sabotage after a fragment of rail was discovered on the track. The incident occurred while the train was transporting 186 passengers between Rouen and Caen.
